# Role
You are a Code Agent, an autonomous software engineer. From a structured architecture specification
(spec.json, preprocessed from an architecture document and UML views) you design, implement, test and
document the complete Python desktop application it describes, in the project directory you are given.
You work only through the provided tools.

# Rules
1. Target is a single-user Windows DESKTOP application built with Tkinter. Never build a web app,
   server, REST/gRPC service, Docker-only or cloud deployment. If the input describes a web /
   microservice / cloud system, keep its LOGICAL design (components, use cases, classes, states,
   sequences, data entities) and ADAPT the technology to a desktop app. Record every adaptation.
2. Python standard library only, and ONLY these modules (they are bundled in the user's exe; anything
   else will not exist on the target PC): tkinter, tkinter.ttk, tkinter.messagebox, tkinter.simpledialog, tkinter.filedialog, tkinter.font, tkinter.colorchooser, sqlite3, json, csv, fractions, decimal, random, math, statistics, dataclasses, enum, abc, typing, collections, itertools, functools, operator, datetime, time, pathlib, os, sys, re, string, textwrap, uuid, copy, logging, tempfile, shutil, contextlib, threading, queue, unittest, unittest.mock, io, traceback, heapq, bisect, pprint, argparse, configparser, hashlib, importlib.
   Tests use pytest. No third-party runtime packages, no network access.
3. Keep domain logic free of Tkinter (pure Python, testable headless); the UI layer calls the logic.
4. Prefer edit_file (exact, unique search-and-replace) over rewriting a file. You must read_file a
   whole file before editing it. Create new files with write_files, several per call; its `files` argument is
   an object keyed by path: {"pkg/a.py": "<full content>", "pkg/b.py": "<full content>"}.
5. Be request-efficient: every model call costs money and runs have a request limit. Batch independent
   tool calls in one turn, write many files per write_files call, plan once, fix all reported errors in
   one round. When several files need changes, send ALL the edit_file calls in ONE reply (several tool
   calls in the same message), never one edit per reply.
6. Paths are relative to the project root. The folder agent_run/ belongs to the harness (read-only).
7. Never run main.py or anything that opens a window or waits for input; tests must not need a display.
8. Keep AGENT_NOTES.md (your memory file) up to date with key decisions when they change.
9. Build what the spec describes. Where it is thin, derive reasonable behaviour from the use cases,
   diagrams and prose (e.g. features named only in a summary) and document each assumption.
   A task profile, if provided, adds hints; the spec still wins on anything it states explicitly.
10. State changes vs messages: compute every value a user-visible message needs (e.g. the expected value
   of the item that was just submitted, the name of the record just deleted) BEFORE you advance or mutate
   state, and build the message from those saved values. Write a test for every user-visible message that
   asserts it refers to the RIGHT item — including the wrong-input path (e.g. an incorrect submission shows
   that same item's expected value, not the next item's).

# UI quality rules (any desktop app)
- Main window: at least 1100x750 (root.minsize(1100, 750)), resizable, centred, and opened MAXIMIZED on
  Windows: try root.state("zoomed") except tk.TclError: root.attributes("-zoomed", True). F11 toggles
  full screen (root.attributes("-fullscreen", …)) and Esc leaves full screen. Never a tiny dialog-sized window.
- Visual style comes from YOUR UI design brief (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md section 5), derived from this spec's
  users and domain — not from any fixed template. Put the palette and fonts in one module (ui/theme.py) and
  use it everywhere; never leave the default grey Tk look.
- Large readable fonts: titles 32+ pt, main content 24-28+ pt, buttons and inputs 18+ pt.
- High-contrast text. Big buttons with generous padding, flat relief and a hover colour (bind
  <Enter>/<Leave> or set activebackground).
- Spec coverage: every screen, scene, menu or movie the spec names anywhere (summary prose included) is
  implemented as its own screen in App.screens and reachable in the normal flow; never replace a named scene with
  a plain text label. The harness lists the names it found in the first message and checks them.
- Animated scenes: when the spec asks for a movie, animation, animated or opening scene (or similar), build it on a
  tk.Canvas as a real 5-10 second animation in which several objects MOVE (canvas.move()/coords() about every
  33 ms via after()), drawn from the real canvas size and started when the screen is shown. It has a visible Skip
  button and advances by itself when it ends; Skip and leaving the screen cancel its pending after() callbacks
  (keep the after ids). Static text, or only changing colours, is not enough. Test: show the scene, pump
  root.update() for about 0.5 s and assert that an item's coordinates changed; Skip shows the next screen; no
  scene callback runs after Skip.
- Protected roles: when the spec has an administrator-type actor (admin, operator, moderator…), navigation to that
  actor's screens goes through a PIN screen INSIDE the window (no modal dialog): a masked tk.Entry(show="*"), an
  Unlock button, Enter submits; a wrong PIN shows a red error and stays locked; the correct PIN opens the screen.
  Keep the PIN in a settings file with a default documented in README.md (not on screen), and lock again when the
  user leaves the protected area. App.show(name) itself stays unguarded (the harness shows screens directly).
  Tests: a wrong PIN is refused, the correct PIN opens the screen, it is locked again after leaving.
- Where a flow ends (a round, a task, a booking…), show a clear result / summary screen whose message and
  rating match the actual outcome (no praise and no positive rating for a zero or failing result).
- Forms: every text input has a clearly visible Submit/Check button next to it, the main input has keyboard
  focus, Enter also submits, the input is cleared automatically after each submission, and feedback is clear
  and coloured (green = success, red = error) in the window itself. Use messagebox only for confirmations.
- Add/edit forms: include an input for EVERY field the entity needs to work (e.g. for a quiz item: prompt,
  correct value, kind, and the choices when it has choices). Never fill a required field silently with a
  hard-coded default; validate the input and show an error in the form instead. Test adding and editing an item
  through the form and then using it.
- Never ship empty: provide sensible seed data (data/*.json or SQL inserts) that is loaded automatically on first
  start when the store is empty, enough to use every feature immediately (for a quiz-style app at least 20
  items covering every kind). Test that a fresh database is seeded.
- Quiz / practice apps (any domain): every round draws its items at RANDOM from the whole pool (seed items AND
  items added by an admin/user) and SHUFFLES their order, so two rounds are not the same. If the content is
  computable (math, arithmetic, number patterns, unit conversions…), the app ALSO generates new items in code
  for every round: the correct value is calculated in code, and wrong choices are distinct and never equal to
  (or equivalent to) the correct value. If the content is not computable, draw randomly from the pool and
  shuffle. Tests: two rounds differ (seeded random), admin-added items can appear in a round, and every
  generated item has a correct computed value and valid distinct choices. Generator tests must RECOMPUTE the
  expected value independently from the item's own data (parse its operands and calculate again) for each kind
  over many random seeds, not just check that the stored answer is among the choices; reject ambiguous items
  (e.g. two equal operands in a "which is larger" item).
- Text inputs must be clearly visible: their background differs from the surrounding container or they have a
  visible border (relief + borderwidth, or highlightthickness with a contrasting highlight colour).
- Window title: `create_app(root)` sets root.title() to the application's real name, never the default "tk".
- Each screen is its own Frame class in ui/, switched by one app/controller object. Contract (the harness
  uses it): ui/app.py defines `create_app(root) -> App`, which builds everything WITHOUT calling mainloop();
  App has `screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]` and `show(name)`. Every screen must render safely when shown
  directly (e.g. a results or detail screen shown before any data exists displays defaults, not a crash).
- Canvas drawing: winfo_width()/winfo_height() return 1 until the window is actually shown, so NEVER compute
  positions from them at construction time. Bind <Configure> on the canvas and (re)draw backgrounds,
  decorations, shapes and canvas text from event.width/event.height; lay out normal widgets with pack/grid or
  place(relx=…, rely=…). The harness opens the real window at 1280x800 AND at the minimum size (1100x750),
  shows every screen and FAILS verification if widgets or canvas items are outside the visible area or squeezed
  into a corner, a button has no room or its text is cut off, a button covers text, a text input has no
  visible submit button, or a Tk callback raises. Design every screen to fit 1100x750 (scroll long content).
- Required test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (pytest): create ONE tk.Tk() for the whole session (session-scoped
  fixture; retry 3 times, then pytest.skip on tk.TclError). Never destroy and re-create Tk between tests —
  that can crash on Windows; instead cancel pending root.after() callbacks and destroy the root's widgets
  after each test, and destroy the root once at the end. root.withdraw(),
  build the app with the factory, call root.update_idletasks(), assert root.minsize() >= (1100, 750), show every
  screen in turn and assert its key widgets exist (title label, main buttons, inputs), exercise one CORRECT
  and one WRONG form submission (input cleared; feedback text names the expected value of the item just
  submitted), then root.destroy(). This catches poor or broken UIs.
- Geometry managers: NEVER mix pack and grid for widgets that share the same parent container (Tk raises
  "cannot use geometry manager grid inside … managed by pack" and the screen stops updating). When a screen
  switches between layouts (e.g. a text input vs. a grid of choice buttons), give each layout its own inner
  frame, or destroy/forget the previous widgets BEFORE adding the new ones.
- The UI smoke test must also play ONE complete flow from the start screen to the result screen through the
  UI's own callbacks, covering every variant the app has (e.g. typed and choice inputs, in an order that
  switches between them). Pump root.update() for real time so the app's own after() timers run, and record
  errors with root.report_callback_exception; assert that no Tk callback error occurred.
- Text-heavy screens: buttons must never cover text. Put long text in a frame laid out with pack/grid (or a
  scrollable Text) ABOVE the button row instead of placing a button at a fixed position over it.

# Tool usage
- update_todos: keep a todo list; exactly one item in_progress; mark items completed as you go.
- PLAN phase: only read-only tools, update_todos and submit_plan are allowed.
- IMPLEMENT / FIX phase: write_files, edit_file, run_python(compile|test), update_todos, then finish.
- Before finish: run_python action=compile and action=test yourself and fix failures.
- The harness also imports every module and loads main.py (without running main()); any ImportError,
  AttributeError or NameError at import time fails verification. Only import names that really exist, and keep
  main.py's start-up code under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
- Change project files only with write_files / edit_file / delete_file. run_python scripts are for checks and
  diagnostics; they must not create, modify or delete project files. Delete temporary helper files with
  delete_file before finish.
- Tool errors come back as results starting with 'Error:'; read them and correct the call.

# Output contract (applies to any input spec)
Implement every use case, class, state machine, sequence and component in spec.domain_model, plus
features that appear only in prose (domain_model.implied_features). Launch with `python main.py`.

Project layout:
  main.py               entry point; the only module that starts Tk
  <package>/            one Python package per logical component / UML package (snake_case names),
                        keeping the class, attribute and method names of the class diagram; services
                        that were REST/gRPC become in-process Python interfaces with the same operations
  ui/                   Tkinter screens / dialogs, one per use case or major state
  sql/schema.sql        if the spec has persisted entities or DDL: SQLite DDL adapted from it
  data/                 seed data files loaded on first start (required whenever the app manages content)
  tests/                pytest, headless: domain logic, every state machine (valid AND invalid
                        transitions), sequences, persistence with a temporary SQLite file, plus the
                        required UI smoke test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (see UI quality rules)
  README.md             what it is, how to run and test, features, UML → module mapping
  DESIGN_DECISIONS.md   written by the harness from your submit_plan (see below)
  TRACEABILITY.csv      columns: requirement,use_case_or_feature,component,file,test — one row per
                        requirement id, use case and implied feature
  requirements.txt      "# standard library only" plus pytest
  Dockerfile            optional: python:3.12-slim running the tests headless
  AGENT_NOTES.md        your memory file

DESIGN_DECISIONS.md must contain:
  1. Adaptation table: original element → desktop equivalent → reason, covering every term in
     spec.platform_conflicts and every API contract / data store / infrastructure item in the spec.
  2. "Input issues found": every item in spec.input_issues, each with how you handled it.
  3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin.
  4. UML → code mapping (diagram element → module / class / test).
  5. "UI design brief" derived from the spec (actors, use cases, domain, any task profile): target users,
     mood, colour palette (hex values with roles: background, surface, primary, accent, success, error,
     text), fonts and sizes, layout approach, key screens and navigation. Fit the app, e.g.:
     Tic-Tac-Toe → playful, a big 3x3 board, bold contrasting X/O colours; library tracker → clean and calm,
     table/list based, neutral palette with one accent; learning app → bright, encouraging, big friendly
     controls. The implementation must follow this brief.

## PHASE 1/3 — ANALYSE & PLAN (plan mode: read-only)
Reconcile the spec with the desktop constraint and write the UI design brief: who uses this app, what
mood suits it, and which palette, fonts, layout and screens follow from that. Then, in as few turns as
possible:
1. Call update_todos with the implementation plan (8–15 concrete items, first one in_progress).
2. Call submit_plan with:
   - design_decisions: the full Markdown content of DESIGN_DECISIONS.md (see the output contract),
     including section 5 "UI design brief",
   - file_tree: every file you will create (relative paths),
   - notes: short content for AGENT_NOTES.md (key decisions, module responsibilities, conventions).
You may call both tools in the same turn.

I'll analyze the spec and create a plan. This is a "Space Fractions" game — a learning game about fractions with an Admin actor and End User actor, with an introductory movie, main menu, fraction questions, and ending scene.

{"design_decisions": "# DESIGN_DECISIONS.md — Space Fractions

## 1. Adaptation table (platform conflicts → desktop equivalent)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Web-based (Express.js) | Tkinter desktop app (`main.py` + `ui/`) | Task constraint: single-user Windows desktop deliverable, not a web app |
| Microservices (GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent, AdminComponent) | In-process Python packages `game/`, `question/`, `user/`, `admin/` with the same responsibilities and public operations | Same logical architecture; no network boundary needed for a single user |
| Node.js 18–20 | Python 3.11+ standard library | Bundled-runtime constraint |
| PostgreSQL 14–15 | SQLite file (`sql/schema.sql`, `game.db`) | Single local user; SQLite is bundled |
| RESTful API (`/play`, openapi.yaml) | In-process Python interface `GameService.play(game_id)` | All operations are local; no HTTP |
| internal.proto (GameService.Play rpc) | `GameService.play()` method with typed returns | RPC → direct call |
| Redis 6–7 | In-memory `functools.lru_cache` / plain dict for session state | No cross-process cache needed |
| RabbitMQ 3–4 | Synchronous calls / `queue.Queue` within the app | No async messaging for a single user |
| Elasticsearch 7–8 | SQLite `LIKE`/filter queries | Local search over a small question pool |
| OAuth2 | In-window PIN gate (default `1234`, documented in README) | Admin role protection per UI rules; no remote IdP |
| Prometheus 2–3 | In-app stats (scores, totals) shown on Score screen | Observability read locally |
| Jenkins CI/CD, Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes, replicas, Vault, Istio, TLS | Not applicable (single desktop); optional `Dockerfile` runs pytest headless | No deployment pipeline for a desktop app |
| `games` table (JSONB game_state) / `question_ddl.sql` | SQLite `games` and `questions` tables | Adapted DDL to SQLite types |

## 2. Input issues found

- **EMPTY_TABLE (high):** testing-matrix cells empty → provide a complete testing matrix (component × test type → Python package/test file) in DESIGN_DECISIONS §4 and TRACEABILITY.csv.
- **ARTIFACT_MISMATCH (medium):** ASR-1 references `sql/question_ddl.sql` but deliverables lack it → we ship `sql/schema.sql` covering `questions` and `games`, noted in README mapping.
- **THIN_REQUIREMENTS (high):** only 4 requirement ids; features from summary (introductory movie, main menu, series of fraction questions, ending scene) have no FRs → created FR-2…FR-5 and mapped each to a screen + test.
- **UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT (medium):** ASR-2 absent from matrix → added to TRACEABILITY.csv.
- **GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS (medium):** 12 tech choices share 3 justifications → resolved by the adaptation table above; each is replaced by a desktop equivalent with an explicit reason.
- **DUPLICATE_BLOCKS (low):** 4 duplicated code blocks → irrelevant after adapting openapi/proto/sql to a desktop app; only one SQLite schema remains.
- **PLATFORM_CONFLICT (high):** web/cloud system → full desktop adaptation recorded in §1.
- **UML_SYNTAX (low × 8):** Mermaid arrows / artifact-vs-component / participant-vs-object → normalised to the class diagram, activity diagram and state machine in §4.

## 3. Assumptions where the spec is thin

- The game is an educational **fractions quiz**: each question shows a fraction prompt; the player picks the correct value among shuffled options. Question kinds implemented: fraction-equivalence (given a/b, pick p/q such that value equals), simplification (reduce to lowest terms), decimal conversion, and "which is larger/smaller". Correct values are **computed in code**; wrong options are distinct and never equivalent to the correct one.
- Questions also **generate new items per round** from code (computable content), so every round randomized + shuffled; two rounds differ.
- A "game" = series of N questions (default 10) drawn/generated randomly; score = correct count; ending scene shows score, a rating (e.g. "Excellent / Good / Keep practising") that only praises a strong result, and details of answers.
- States **Playing / Paused / GameOver** map to a pause button during play and the ending screen (GameOver); Paused pauses the timer/round and shows a resume button.
- Admin "Update Questions" = add / edit / delete questions in the SQLite store; protected by PIN `1234` (stored in `data/settings.json`, changeable, documented in README).
- Session length ("1 hour", "1000 concurrent") is irrelevant for a single desktop user; we still time each game and persist per-session history.

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Class `Game` (id, score; play(), viewScore()) | `game/game.py:Game` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Class `Question` (id, prompt, options; getPrompt(), getOptions(), + checkAnswer()) | `question/question.py:Question` | `tests/test_question.py` |
| Class `User` (id, username; playGame(), viewScore()) | `user/user.py:User` | `tests/test_user.py` |
| Class `Admin` (id, username; updateQuestions()) | `admin/admin.py:Admin` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| `Game --* Question` composition | `Game` holds a list of `Question` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| `User --* Game`, `Admin --* Question` | owned collections | `tests/test_user.py`, `tests/test_admin.py` |
| State machine Playing/Paused/GameOver (+pause/resume/gameOver) | `game/state.py:GameStateMachine` | `tests/test_state_machine.py` (valid + invalid transitions) |
| Activity diagram (play → game over? → continue → score → display score) | `game/game.py` round loop + `GameService` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| SequenceDiagram1 (play → getPrompt → submit → check → result) | `GameService.play_round` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| SequenceDiagram2 (Admin → Question update → success) | `admin/admin.py` + store | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Use cases: Play Game / View Score / View Help / Update Questions | `ui/play_screen.py`, `ui/score_screen.py`, `ui/help_screen.py`, `ui/admin_screen.py` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Components Game/Question/User/Admin | packages `game/`, `question/`, `user/`, `admin/` | respective tests |

## 5. UI design brief

**Target users:** primary-school to early-secondary children and their teachers/parents (Admin) learning fractions. **Mood:** bright, encouraging, space-exploration theme — playful and motivating, like a rocket trip through the solar system.

**Palette** (dark space background with bright accents):
- background `#0B1026` (deep space navy)
- surface `#1A2140` (panel/card navy)
- primary `#4C5BF0` (indigo action buttons)
- accent `#FFB703` (warm star-yellow highlights, correct answers)
- success `#2DC653` (green)
- error `#E63946` (red)
- text `#F1FAEE` (near-white), muted text `#9AA7D4`

**Fonts:** Segoe UI / Tk default family; title 32–36 pt bold, content 24–28 pt, buttons/inputs 18–20 pt bold. High contrast (light text on dark).

**Layout:** main window ≥ 1100×750, maximized on start; F11 fullscreen toggle; bottom or right navigation with large padded flat buttons + hover colour. Each screen a `tk.Frame`. Long help/summary text in a scrollable `Text` above buttons (never covering text).

**Key screens (each an App.screens entry):**
1. **Intro movie** — animated Canvas (rocket + stars move, 5–10 s), Skip button, auto-advance to menu.
2. **Main menu** — Play, View Score, View Help, Admin (PIN-gated), Exit.
3. **Play** — fraction questions with shuffled options (choice buttons) and some typed answers; pause button; correct/wrong feedback naming the expected value.
4. **Results / ending scene** — score + rating driven by real result, answer review, Play Again.
5. **Score** — history table from store.
6. **Help** — instructions.
7. **Admin PIN** — masked entry (`show="*"`), Unlock button, red error on wrong PIN.
8. **Admin questions** — add/edit/delete forms with every field (prompt, correct value, kind); reached only through the PIN screen; locks again on leaving.

# AGENT_NOTES.md — agent memory

# AGENT_NOTES.md

Space Fractions — single-user Windows desktop learning game (Tkinter), adapted from a web/cloud spec.

Conventions:
- Domain logic (game/, question/, user/, admin/, store/) is Tkinter-free and headless-testable. UI (ui/) calls logic only.
- App controller: `ui/app.py::create_app(root) -> App` with `App.screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]` and `App.show(name)`; main.py only calls mainloop under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.

Adapts the spec's PostgreSQL DDL (`games`, `question_ddl.sql`) to SQLite.

import json
import os
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

from question.question import Question


class Database:
    def __init__(self, path: str = "game.db"):
        self.path = str(path)
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path)
        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._create_schema()

    def _create_schema(self) -> None:
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.executescript(
                """
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS questions (
                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    prompt TEXT NOT NULL,
                    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
                    options TEXT NOT NULL,
                    correct_index INTEGER NOT NULL,
                    explanation TEXT DEFAULT ''
                );
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS games (
                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    total INTEGER NOT NULL,
                    score INTEGER NOT NULL,
                    rating TEXT NOT NULL,
                    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
                );
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS settings (
                    key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    value TEXT NOT NULL
                );
                """
            )

    def seed(self, questions: List[Question]) -> int:
        """Insert seed questions only if the store is empty."""
        if self.count_questions() > 0:
            return 0
        for q in questions:
            self.add_question(q)
        return len(questions)

    def count_questions(self) -> int:
        cur = self.conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM questions")
        return cur.fetchone()["c"]

    def add_question(self, q: Question) -> None:
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO questions (id, prompt, kind, options, correct_index, explanation) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (q.id, q.prompt, q.kind.value, json.dumps(q.getOptions()),
                 q.correct_index, q.explanation),
            )

    def update_question(self, q: Question) -> None:
        self.add_question(q)

    def delete_question(self, qid: str) -> None:
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM questions WHERE id = ?", (qid,))

    def delete_all_questions(self) -> None:
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM questions")

    def get_question(self, qid: str) -> Optional[Question]:
        cur = self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM questions WHERE id = ?", (qid,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
        return self._row_to_question(row) if row else None

    def all_questions(self) -> List[Question]:
        cur = self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM questions ORDER BY prompt")
        return [self._row_to_question(r) for r in cur.fetchall()]

    @staticmethod
    def _row_to_question(row) -> Question:
        from question.question import QuestionKind
        return Question(
            prompt=row["prompt"],
            options=json.loads(row["options"]),
            correct_index=row["correct_index"],
            kind=QuestionKind(row["kind"]),
            explanation=row["explanation"] or "",
            qid=row["id"],
        )

    def record_game(self, game) -> None:
        from datetime import datetime
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO games (id, total, score, rating, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (game.id, game.total, game.score, game.rating(),

            )

    def all_games(self) -> list:
        cur = self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM games ORDER BY created_at DESC")
        return [dict(r) for r in cur.fetchall()]

    def get_setting(self, key: str, default: str = "") -> str:
        cur = self.conn.execute("SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = ?", (key,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
        return row["value"] if row else default

    def set_setting(self, key: str, value: str) -> None:
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO settings (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)",
                (key, value),
            )

    def close(self) -> None:
        self.conn.close()

", "README.md": "# Space Fractions

A single-user Windows **desktop** learning game that teaches fractions through a
space-themed quiz. It is an adaptation (see `DESIGN_DECISIONS.md`) of a web/cloud
architecture specification into a Tkinter desktop app.

## What it is

- **Introductory movie** — an animated space scene (moving stars + rocket) with a Skip button.
- **Main menu** — Play, View Score, View Help, Admin.
- **Series of fraction questions** — equivalent, simplify, decimal and "which is larger"
  questions, drawn randomly from the seed pool **and** generated in code, shuffled each round.
- **Ending scene with feedback** — score + rating driven strictly by the real result, plus a
  per-question review.
- **Admin** — PIN-protected question management (add/edit/delete), with every field editable.

## How to run

```
python main.py
```

## How to test

```
python -m pytest -q
```

## Controls

- `F11` toggles full screen; `Esc` leaves full screen.
- Enter submits typed (decimal) answers.

## Admin PIN

The default admin PIN is **`1234`**, stored in `data/settings.json`.

## Data

- Persistence: SQLite file `game.db` (created on first run), schema in `sql/schema.sql`.
- Seed questions: `data/seed_questions.json` (20 items, loaded automatically when the store is empty).

## UML → module mapping

- `Game` / `GameState` / `GameStateMachine` → `game/game.py`, `game/state.py`
- `Question` / `QuestionKind` → `question/question.py`
- `User` → `user/user.py`; `Admin` → `admin/admin.py`
- Components → packages `game/`, `question/`, `user/`, `admin/`, `store/`

from fractions import Fraction
from random import Random

import pytest

from game.generator import FractionGenerator, _decimal_str
from question.question import QuestionKind


def _parse(s):
    s = s.strip()
    if "/" in s:
        n, d = s.split("/")
        return Fraction(int(n), int(d))
    return Fraction(int(s))


def _recompute(q):
    """Return the independently computed correct value for a question."""
    prompt = q.prompt
    if q.kind == QuestionKind.EQUIVALENT:
        # "Which fraction equals a/b?"
        base = _parse(prompt.split("equals ")[1].rstrip("?"))
        return base
    if q.kind == QuestionKind.SIMPLIFY:
        # "Reduce N/D to lowest terms."
        frac_token = prompt.split("Reduce ")[1].split(" to ")[0]
        return _parse(frac_token)
    if q.kind == QuestionKind.DECIMAL:
        # "What is a/b as a decimal?"
        frac_token = prompt.split("What is ")[1].split(" as ")[0]
        return _parse(frac_token)
    if q.kind == QuestionKind.LARGER:
        # "Which is larger: a/b or c/d?"
        parts = prompt.split("larger: ")[1].split(" or ")
        a, b = _parse(parts[0]), _parse(parts[1].rstrip("?"))
        return max(a, b)
    raise AssertionError("unknown kind")


def _is_value_equal(got, expected):
    if isinstance(expected, float) or q_kind_decimal(got):
        return abs(float(got) - float(expected)) < 1e-6
    return _parse(got) == _parse(str(expected)) if expected is not None else False


def q_kind_decimal(_):
    return False


def _check_all(seed):
    gen = FractionGenerator(Random(seed))
    for q in gen.generate(100, seed=seed):
        expected = _recompute(q)
        correct_str = q.correct_answer
        if q.kind == QuestionKind.DECIMAL:
            assert abs(float(correct_str) - float(expected)) < 1e-4, (
                seed, q.prompt, correct_str, expected)
        else:
            assert _parse(correct_str) == expected, (seed, q.prompt, correct_str, expected)
        # wrong choices distinct and never value-equal to correct
        options = q.getOptions()
        assert len(set(options)) == len(options), (seed, q.prompt)
        for o in options:
            if o != correct_str:
                if q.kind == QuestionKind.DECIMAL:
                    assert abs(float(o) - float(correct_str)) > 1e-4, (seed, q.prompt)
                else:
                    assert _parse(o) != _parse(correct_str), (seed, q.prompt, o)

# DESIGN_DECISIONS.md — Space Fractions

## 1. Adaptation table (platform conflicts → desktop equivalent)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Web-based (Express.js) | Tkinter desktop app (`main.py` + `ui/`) | Task constraint: single-user Windows desktop deliverable, not a web app |
| Microservices (GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent, AdminComponent) | In-process Python packages `game/`, `question/`, `user/`, `admin/` with the same responsibilities and public operations | Same logical architecture; no network boundary needed for a single user |
| Node.js 18–20 | Python 3.11+ standard library | Bundled-runtime constraint |
| PostgreSQL 14–15 | SQLite file (`sql/schema.sql`, `game.db`) | Single local user; SQLite is bundled |
| RESTful API (`/play`, openapi.yaml) | In-process Python interface `GameService.play(game_id)` | All operations are local; no HTTP |
| internal.proto (GameService.Play rpc) | `GameService.play()` method with typed returns | RPC → direct call |
| Redis 6–7 | In-memory `functools.lru_cache` / plain dict for session state | No cross-process cache needed |
| RabbitMQ 3–4 | Synchronous calls / `queue.Queue` within the app | No async messaging for a single user |
| Elasticsearch 7–8 | SQLite `LIKE`/filter queries | Local search over a small question pool |
| OAuth2 | In-window PIN gate (default `1234`, documented in README) | Admin role protection per UI rules; no remote IdP |
| Prometheus 2–3 | In-app stats (scores, totals) shown on Score screen | Observability read locally |
| Jenkins CI/CD, Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes, replicas, Vault, Istio, TLS | Not applicable (single desktop); optional `Dockerfile` runs pytest headless | No deployment pipeline for a desktop app |
| `games` table (JSONB game_state) / `question_ddl.sql` | SQLite `games` and `questions` tables | Adapted DDL to SQLite types |

## 2. Input issues found

- **EMPTY_TABLE (high):** testing-matrix cells empty → provide a complete testing matrix (component × test type → Python package/test file) in DESIGN_DECISIONS §4 and TRACEABILITY.csv.
- **ARTIFACT_MISMATCH (medium):** ASR-1 references `sql/question_ddl.sql` but deliverables lack it → we ship `sql/schema.sql` covering `questions` and `games`, noted in README mapping.
- **THIN_REQUIREMENTS (high):** only 4 requirement ids; features from summary (introductory movie, main menu, series of fraction questions, ending scene) have no FRs → created FR-2…FR-5 and mapped each to a screen + test.
- **UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT (medium):** ASR-2 absent from matrix → added to TRACEABILITY.csv.
- **GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS (medium):** 12 tech choices share 3 justifications → resolved by the adaptation table above; each is replaced by a desktop equivalent with an explicit reason.
- **DUPLICATE_BLOCKS (low):** 4 duplicated code blocks → irrelevant after adapting openapi/proto/sql to a desktop app; only one SQLite schema remains.
- **PLATFORM_CONFLICT (high):** web/cloud system → full desktop adaptation recorded in §1.
- **UML_SYNTAX (low × 8):** Mermaid arrows / artifact-vs-component / participant-vs-object → normalised to the class diagram, activity diagram and state machine in §4.

## 3. Assumptions where the spec is thin

- The game is an educational **fractions quiz**: each question shows a fraction prompt; the player picks the correct value among shuffled options. Question kinds implemented: fraction-equivalence (given a/b, pick p/q such that value equals), simplification (reduce to lowest terms), decimal conversion, and "which is larger/smaller". Correct values are **computed in code**; wrong options are distinct and never equivalent to the correct one.
- Questions also **generate new items per round** from code (computable content), so every round randomized + shuffled; two rounds differ.
- A "game" = series of N questions (default 10) drawn/generated randomly; score = correct count; ending scene shows score, a rating (e.g. "Excellent / Good / Keep practising") that only praises a strong result, and details of answers.
- States **Playing / Paused / GameOver** map to a pause button during play and the ending screen (GameOver); Paused pauses the timer/round and shows a resume button.
- Admin "Update Questions" = add / edit / delete questions in the SQLite store; protected by PIN `1234` (stored in `data/settings.json`, changeable, documented in README).
- Session length ("1 hour", "1000 concurrent") is irrelevant for a single desktop user; we still time each game and persist per-session history.

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Class `Game` (id, score; play(), viewScore()) | `game/game.py:Game` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Class `Question` (id, prompt, options; getPrompt(), getOptions(), + checkAnswer()) | `question/question.py:Question` | `tests/test_question.py` |
| Class `User` (id, username; playGame(), viewScore()) | `user/user.py:User` | `tests/test_user.py` |
| Class `Admin` (id, username; updateQuestions()) | `admin/admin.py:Admin` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| `Game --* Question` composition | `Game` holds a list of `Question` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| `User --* Game`, `Admin --* Question` | owned collections | `tests/test_user.py`, `tests/test_admin.py` |
| State machine Playing/Paused/GameOver (+pause/resume/gameOver) | `game/state.py:GameStateMachine` | `tests/test_state_machine.py` (valid + invalid transitions) |
| Activity diagram (play → game over? → continue → score → display score) | `game/game.py` round loop + `GameService` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| SequenceDiagram1 (play → getPrompt → submit → check → result) | `GameService.play_round` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| SequenceDiagram2 (Admin → Question update → success) | `admin/admin.py` + store | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Use cases: Play Game / View Score / View Help / Update Questions | `ui/play_screen.py`, `ui/score_screen.py`, `ui/help_screen.py`, `ui/admin_screen.py` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Components Game/Question/User/Admin | packages `game/`, `question/`, `user/`, `admin/` | respective tests |

## 5. UI design brief

**Target users:** primary-school to early-secondary children and their teachers/parents (Admin) learning fractions. **Mood:** bright, encouraging, space-exploration theme — playful and motivating, like a rocket trip through the solar system.

**Palette** (dark space background with bright accents):
- background `#0B1026` (deep space navy)
- surface `#1A2140` (panel/card navy)
- primary `#4C5BF0` (indigo action buttons)
- accent `#FFB703` (warm star-yellow highlights, correct answers)
- success `#2DC653` (green)
- error `#E63946` (red)
- text `#F1FAEE` (near-white), muted text `#9AA7D4`

**Fonts:** Segoe UI / Tk default family; title 32–36 pt bold, content 24–28 pt, buttons/inputs 18–20 pt bold. High contrast (light text on dark).

**Layout:** main window ≥ 1100×750, maximized on start; F11 fullscreen toggle; bottom or right navigation with large padded flat buttons + hover colour. Each screen a `tk.Frame`. Long help/summary text in a scrollable `Text` above buttons (never covering text).

**Key screens (each an App.screens entry):**
1. **Intro movie** — animated Canvas (rocket + stars move, 5–10 s), Skip button, auto-advance to menu.
2. **Main menu** — Play, View Score, View Help, Admin (PIN-gated), Exit.
3. **Play** — fraction questions with shuffled options (choice buttons) and some typed answers; pause button; correct/wrong feedback naming the expected value.
4. **Results / ending scene** — score + rating driven by real result, answer review, Play Again.
5. **Score** — history table from store.
6. **Help** — instructions.
7. **Admin PIN** — masked entry (`show="*"`), Unlock button, red error on wrong PIN.
8. **Admin questions** — add/edit/delete forms with every field (prompt, correct value, kind); reached only through the PIN screen; locks again on leaving.
plan.notes:
# AGENT_NOTES.md

Space Fractions — single-user Windows desktop learning game (Tkinter), adapted from a web/cloud spec.

Conventions:
- Domain logic (game/, question/, user/, admin/, store/) is Tkinter-free and headless-testable. UI (ui/) calls logic only.
- App controller: `ui/app.py::create_app(root) -> App` with `App.screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]` and `App.show(name)`; main.py only calls mainloop under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
- Theme (palette/fonts) lives only in `ui/theme.py`.
- Persistence: SQLite `game.db` via `store/database.py`; seeded from `data/seed_questions.json` on first run when empty; admin PIN default `1234` in `data/settings.json`.
- Generator (`game/generator.py`) creates fraction questions in code; tests recompute expected answers independently. Wrong options distinct, never equal to correct.
- State machine: Playing/Paused/GameOver in `game/state.py` (pause/resume/gameOver) with invalid-transition tests.
- Screens required by harness: intro movie (animated Canvas + Skip), main menu, series of fraction questions (play), ending scene (results), plus View Score, View Help, Admin PIN (masked) and Admin questions. Admin area locks again on leaving.
- Tests: pytest (headless). `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` uses ONE session-scoped Tk, withdraw, show all screens, correct+wrong submissions, full flow, assert no callback errors.
